notes: Graded by Claude/Opus reading all 15 full-length answers. Weights: correctness 0.35, depth 0.25, instruction_following 0.20, practicality 0.20. All three quants are excellent and near-equivalent; differences are small and consistent (Q8 >= Q6 >= Q5). q1 (market research) is uniformly capped on correctness because the local model's training cutoff predates the real mid-2026 models (it recommends speculative 'Qwen3-32B', and several answers wrongly claim 'MTP not supported, skip').

scores.rationale: Sound reasoning and a coincidentally-near-correct pick (Qwen ~30B at Q5), but cutoff-limited: speculative model names and the wrong claim that MTP isn't supported. Covers all parts (research, comparison, pick, hosting, wiring).
Correct token-bucket + worker-pool + retry/jitter + abort + failure isolation. Minor: no max-backoff cap, and an items[index-1] edge bug in the fallback catch.
Excellent, audit-first design: provenance map, hash-chained audit log, replay(), strict compute-then-narrate boundary with a verifier gate. Independently mirrors the real engine's principles.
Sophisticated second-order reasoning (CoWoS/packaging bottleneck, inference commoditization, grid resilience), clean signal-vs-noise table and sector matrix, actionable weekly plan.
Sharp: correctly notes the original code doesn't actually cache rejections and the poisoning emerges from the naive fix. Correct dedup-before-await + .catch eviction + TTL/LRU.
More decisive than q5 with explicit memory math and a 'don't trust native function-calling, route via JSON' caveat that matches reality. Still cutoff-limited/speculative on model names.
Cleanest structure: modular retryWithBackoff + abortable delay helpers, worker pool, collects results. Correct and idiomatic; abort not counted as failure.
Most concrete architecture: SQL DDL for the job registry, advisory-lock overlap prevention, idempotency keys, Merkle-root lineage, verifier gate. Production-grade.
Strong 'scissors effect' framing (rising input costs vs falling inference prices), explicit hedges and trigger levels for the week. Crisp prioritized summary.
Correct analysis and a clean minimal fix plus a generic AsyncCache (TTL + LRU). Slightly more concise than q5; notes cross-worker/distributed caveats.
The most complete q1: capability matrix, RAG strategy, full engine wiring with code, operational checklist, fallback plan. Still cutoff-limited; minor slip ('Q6_K pushes past 45GB').
Most complete coding answer: adds a maxDelayMs backoff cap and tracks retries in errors. Correct throughout; tiny unused destructure of {retries}.
Comprehensive: provenance ids, hash-chained audit, DLQ, idempotency keys, advisory locks, network-isolated narration container. Every digest line resolves to a number or dated source.
Adds explicit cross-sector feedback loops and resolves the apparent HBM-up/inference-down paradox via software efficiency + workload tiering. Tightest reasoning of the three.
Cleanest fix: a createLoader factory that also wraps Promise.resolve(fetchFn()) to catch SYNCHRONOUS throws (a subtlety the others missed), plus TTL + FIFO eviction and stampede note.
